question: Como usar utc=True em to_datetime com offsets?
reference_facts: utc normaliza/converte timezone conforme entradas; não inventar fuso original.

claims.text: Para usar `utc=True` em `pd.to_datetime`, é necessário especificar esse parâmetro para garantir que os dados sejam sempre interpretados como timezone-aware UTC. Isso localiza ou converte os valores de entrada para UTC, independentemente de serem timezone-naive ou timezone-aware. O uso de `utc=True` é recomendado para evitar erros em versões futuras do pandas quando houver dados com fusos horários mistos.

evidence_quotes.quote:
utc bool, default False
In a future version of pandas, parsing datetimes with mixed time
zones will raise an error unless utc=True.
Please specify utc=True to opt in to the new behaviour
and silence this warning. To create a Series with mixed offsets and
object dtype, please use apply and datetime.datetime.strptime.

See also: pandas general documentation about [timezone conversion and\\
localization](https://pandas.pydata.org/pandas-docs/stable/user_guide/timeseries.html#time-zone-handling).

utc bool, default False

Control timezone-related parsing, localization and conversion.

- If `True`, the function _always_ returns a timezone-aware
UTC-localized `Timestamp`, `Series` or
`DatetimeIndex`. To do this, timezone-naive inputs are
_localized_ as UTC, while timezone-aware inputs are _converted_ to UTC.

- If `False` (default), inputs will not be coerced to UTC.
Timezone-naive inputs will remain naive, while timezone-aware ones
will keep their time offsets. Limitations exist for mixed
offsets (typically, daylight savings), see Examples section for details.

Warning
